'''Piecewise linear interpolation''' is the process of finding a series of linear functions $L_i(x)$ that for a definite set of datapoints $\{(x_i,y_i)|\ i\in [0,n], i \in N\}$ satisfies $L(x_i)=y_i$.

i.e., find

$$
L(x)=L_i(x),\, x_i \le x \le x_{i+1} \forall \{(x_i,y_i)| i\in [0,n], i \in N\} \\
L_i(x)=a_i(x-x_i)+b_i
$$

== Solution ==

By definition,

$$
L_i(x_i)=y_i,\, L_i(x_{i+1})=y_{i+1}
$$

Hence

$$
a_i=\frac{y_{i+1}-y_i}{x_{i+1}-x_i},\, b_i=y_i
$$
